title: ASR-Style Transcript Normalization Removes Useful Pragmatic Signal for Dialogue Act Classification
abstract: arXiv:2610.22934v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) pipelines often normalize transcripts by removing filled pauses and punctuation and expanding colloquial forms, potentially discarding cues useful for dialogue act classification. We evaluate nine transcript conditions across six classifiers (TF-IDF logistic regression, RoBERTa, BERT, ALBERT, GPT-2, and BiLSTM) and three conversational corpora (Switchboard, ICSI MRDA, and SLUE-HVB), supplemented by multi-seed experiments, normalization controls, and real-ASR evaluations. Across five random seeds, heavy normalization reduces Macro-F1 in all 15 neural model-corpus combinations under the original preprocessing protocols. Removal using the original filler and backchannel lexicon consistently degrades performance on MRDA and SLUE-HVB but produces mixed effects on Switchboard. tldr: 研究通过对六种分类器和三个会话语料库的系统性实验证明，ASR流水线中常见的转录规范化操作（如移除填充词和标点符号）会持续降低对话行为分类性能，表明这些语言特征包含重要的语用信号。
en_tdlr: Systematic experiments across six classifiers and three conversational corpora show that common ASR transcript normalization practices (removing fillers and punctuation) consistently degrade dialogue act classification performance, indicating these linguistic features carry important pragmatic signals.
